title: The Ledger of Greywater Bay
premise: Bram Crane, Greywater Bay's unassuming coroner, has spent years quietly correcting the record on deaths ruled accidental. When a drowned man washes up wearing clothes stolen from her own closet, she realizes someone is staging her into a crime she didn't commit—and that the victim is connected to three old cases she once solved in secret. Following a trail of forged alibis back to the summer thirty years ago when her own father's death was ruled an accident, Bram uncovers a conspiracy among the town's founding families to protect an inheritance built on a murder. In the end, she must choose between exposing the truth and preserving the fragile loyalty of the one ally who has protected her all along—her mentor, Sheriff Ada Voss—who finally confesses she falsified the original report to shield Bram from a killer who is now dead.
about_author: Noor Sandoval is a former death registrar from a coastal town who spent a decade cataloguing misfiled causes of death before turning to fiction. She writes mysteries about people whose quiet competence makes them dangerous to the powerful.

chapters.title: The Wrong Man's Coat
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. A drowned stranger surfaces at Greywater Bay wearing Bram's own missing coat and scarf, planted like a signature. Police circle her as a suspect; her private history of solving 'accidents' begins leaking. The emotional beat is violated privacy—the woman who knew every grave now fears becoming one. She finds a laundry tag linking the clothes to the Voss household.

chapters.title: Thirty Years of Alibis
chapters.summary: Bram's POV, with interleaved pages from her father's coroner logbook. Digging into the drowned man's identity, she discovers he was a witness to her father's fatal 'accident' in 1994, paid annually by the Harrow family trust. The beat is dread compounding into resolve as she maps how three of her solved cases all trace back to the same inheritance. Sheriff Voss warns her off, oddly protective.

chapters.title: The Statute's Last Week
chapters.summary: Dual POV: Bram and the dying patriarch Elias Harrow. With days before the statute expires, Bram corners Elias, who admits the conspiracy but claims the killer acted alone and is long dead. The climax breaks when Bram realizes the current threats bear fresh fingerprints—someone alive is still protecting the secret. Voss arrests Bram on planted evidence; betrayal lands hardest here.

chapters.title: What the Water Keeps
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. From holding cells and archives, she reconstructs the final night: Voss, then a young deputy, covered for Bram's father's true killer—her father's own partner—to save young Bram from retaliation. Resolution comes through confession rather than conviction: Voss testifies, the trust dissolves, and Bram buries the last nameless grave. The beat is grief braided with loyalty, and peace earned at a cost.
